contents.html: Appendix C: Prime-Factor Recovery (Normative)
contents.html_ja: 付録C：素因数の復元（規範）

contents.html: Two methods for prime-factor recovery are provided below: Appendix C.1 provides a probabilistic method, and Appendix C.2 provides a determinitic method. Prime-factor recovery is required during key-pair validation using the basic format (see Section 6.4.1.2.1).
contents.html_ja: 以下に素因数復元の2つの方法を示す。付録C.1は確率的方法、付録C.2は決定論的方法を示す。基本形式を用いる鍵ペア検証では、素因数の復元が必要である（第6.4.1.2.1節参照）。

contents.html: C.1 Probabilistic Prime-Factor Recovery
contents.html_ja: C.1 確率的素因数復元

contents.html:
The following algorithm recovers the prime factors of a modulus, given the public and private exponents. The algorithm is based on Fact 1 in [Boneh 1999].
Function call: \(\mathrm{RecoverPrimeFactors}(n, e, d)\)
Input:
contents.html_ja:
次のアルゴリズムは、公開指数と秘密指数から法の素因数を復元する。このアルゴリズムは[Boneh 1999]の事実1に基づく。
関数呼び出し： \(\mathrm{RecoverPrimeFactors}(n, e, d)\)
入力：

source_check.observations: 本文、RecoverPrimeFactors(n,e,d)、Input が一致。日本語も同一。

contents.html: 1. \(n\): modulus.

source_check.observations: 1. n: modulus を確認。日本語も同一。

contents.html: 2. \(e\): public exponent.

source_check.observations: 2. e: public exponent を確認。日本語も同一。

contents.html: 3. \(d\): private exponent.

source_check.observations: 3. d: private exponent を確認。日本語も同一。

contents.html: Output:
contents.html_ja: 出力：

contents.html: 1. \((p, q)\): prime factors of modulus.

source_check.observations: 1. (p,q): prime factors of modulus を確認。日本語も同一。

contents.html:
Errors: “prime factors not found”
Assumptions: The modulus \(n\) is the product of two prime factors \(p\) and \(q\); the public and private exponents satisfy \(de \equiv 1 \pmod{\lambda(n)}\) where \(\lambda(n) = \operatorname{LCM}(p - 1, q - 1)\).
contents.html_ja:
エラー：「素因数が見つからない」
前提条件：法\(n\)は2つの素因数\(p\)および\(q\)の積であり、公開指数と秘密指数は\(de \equiv 1 \pmod{\lambda(n)}\)を満たす。ここで\(\lambda(n) = \operatorname{LCM}(p - 1, q - 1)\)である。

source_check.observations: Errors/Assumptions、n,p,q、de≡1 (mod λ(n))、λ(n)=LCM(p−1,q−1) が一致。日本語も同一。

contents.html: Process:
contents.html_ja: 処理：

contents.html: 1. Let \(m = de - 1\). If \(m\) is odd, then go to Step 4.
contents.html_ja: 1. \(m = de - 1\)とする。\(m\)が奇数ならステップ4へ進む。

source_check.observations: m=de−1、m が奇数なら Step 4 が一致。日本語も同一。

contents.html: 2. Write \(m\) as \(m = 2^{t}r\), where \(r\) is the largest odd integer dividing \(m\), and \(t \ge 1\).
contents.html_ja: 2. \(m\)を\(m = 2^{t}r\)と表す。ここで\(r\)は\(m\)を割り切る最大の奇数であり、\(t \ge 1\)である。

source_check.observations: m=2^t r、r は最大の奇数、t≥1 が一致。日本語も同一。
For i=1 to 100 do を確認。日本語も同一。

contents.html:
a. Generate a random integer \(g\) in the range \([0, n-1]\).
b. Let \(y = g^{r} \bmod n\).
c. If \(y = 1\) or \(y = n - 1\), then go to Step g.
d. For \(j = 1\) to \(t - 1\) do:
contents.html_ja:
a. ランダムな整数\(g\)を範囲\([0, n-1]\)から生成する。
b. \(y = g^{r} \bmod n\)とする。
c. \(y = 1\)または\(y = n - 1\)ならステップgへ進む。
d. \(j = 1\)から\(t - 1\)まで繰り返す。

source_check.observations: a〜d、[0,n−1]、y=g^r mod n、y=1 or y=n−1、j=1 to t−1 が一致。日本語も同一。

contents.html:
i. Let \(x = y^{2} \bmod n\).
ii. If \(x = 1\), go to Step 5.
iii. If \(x = n - 1\), go to Step g.
iv. Let \(y = x\).
contents.html_ja:
i. \(x = y^{2} \bmod n\)とする。
ii. \(x = 1\)ならステップ5へ進む。
iii. \(x = n - 1\)ならステップgへ進む。
iv. \(y = x\)とする。

source_check.observations: i〜iv の x=y^2 mod n、x=1→Step 5、x=n−1→Step g、y=x が一致。日本語も同一。

contents.html: e. Let x = y2 mod n. f. If x = 1, go to Step 5. g. Continue.
contents.html_ja: e. x = y^2 mod nとする。 f. x = 1ならステップ5へ進む。 g. 続行する。

contents.html: Output “prime factors not found,” and exit without further processing.
contents.html_ja: 「素因数が見つからない」を出力し、それ以上処理せず終了する。

contents.html: 5. Let \(p = \operatorname{GCD}(y - 1, n)\) and let \(q = n/p\).
contents.html_ja: 5. \(p = \operatorname{GCD}(y - 1, n)\)とし、\(q = n/p\)とする。

source_check.observations: p=GCD(y−1,n)、q=n/p が一致。日本語も同一。

contents.html: 6. Output \((p, q)\) as the prime factors.
contents.html_ja: 6. \((p, q)\)を素因数として出力する。

source_check.observations: 6. Output (p,q) as the prime factors を確認。日本語も同一。

contents.html: Any local copies of \(d\), \(p\), \(q\), \(m\), \(t\), \(r\), \(x\), \(y\), \(g\) and any intermediate values used during the execution of the RecoverPrimeFactors function shall be destroyed prior to or during steps 4 and 6. Note that this includes the values for \(p\) and \(q\) that are output in step 6.
contents.html_ja: RecoverPrimeFactors関数の実行中に使用した\(d\)、\(p\)、\(q\)、\(m\)、\(t\)、\(r\)、\(x\)、\(y\)、\(g\)および中間値のローカルコピーは、ステップ4および6の前または実行中に破棄しなければならない。これには、ステップ6で出力される\(p\)および\(q\)の値も含まれることに注意する。

source_check.observations: d,p,q,m,t,r,x,y,g、steps 4 and 6、p,q、shall が一致。日本語も同一。

contents.html: Notes:
contents.html_ja: 注記：

contents.html: 1. According to Fact 1 in [Boneh 1999], the probability that one of the values of \(y\) in an iteration of Step 3 reveals the factors of the modulus is at least \(1/2\), so on average, no more than two iterations of that step will be required. If the prime factors are not revealed after \(100\) iterations, then the probability is overwhelming that the modulus is not the product of two prime factors, or that the public and private exponents are not consistent with each other.

contents.html:
Lemma 1: \(\operatorname{GCD}(p - 1, q - 1) = \operatorname{GCD}(n - 1, \lambda(n))\)
Proof of Lemma 1:
Since \(n - 1 = (p - 1)(q - 1) + (p - 1) + (q - 1)\) and \(\lambda(n)\) is a divisor of \((p - 1)(q - 1)\), it follows that \(\operatorname{GCD}(n - 1, \lambda(n)) = \operatorname{GCD}((p - 1) + (q - 1), \lambda(n))\).
Any common divisor of \(p - 1\) and \(q - 1\) will also be a divisor of both \((p - 1) + (q - 1)\) and \(\lambda(n)\), and hence a divisor of \(\operatorname{GCD}((p - 1) + (q - 1), \lambda(n))\). In particular, \(\operatorname{GCD}(p - 1, q - 1)\) is a divisor of \(\operatorname{GCD}((p - 1) + (q - 1), \lambda(n))\), and so, \(\operatorname{GCD}(p - 1, q - 1) \le \operatorname{GCD}((p - 1) + (q - 1), \lambda(n))\).
To establish that \(\operatorname{GCD}((p - 1) + (q - 1), \lambda(n)) \le \operatorname{GCD}(p - 1, q - 1)\) – and hence that the two GCDs are equal. Let \(\{\, h_i \mid 1 \le i \le m \,\}\) denote the set of primes that are divisors of either \(p - 1\) or \(q - 1\). Then the factorizations of \(p - 1\), \(q - 1\), and \(\lambda(n)\) have the forms

contents.html: Suppose that \(j\) is also a divisor of \((p - 1) + (q - 1)\) and that, for a particular value of \(i\), \(z(i) = x(i)\). In this case, \(h_i^{w(i)}\) will divide both \(p - 1\) and the sum \((p - 1) + (q - 1)\), hence \(h_i^{w(i)}\) will divide their difference, \(q - 1\). Similarly, if \(z(i) = y(i)\), then \(h_i^{w(i)}\) will divide both \(q - 1\) and the sum \((p - 1) + (q - 1)\), hence \(h_i^{w(i)}\) will divide \(p - 1\) as well. Thus, each prime-power factor of \(j\) is a common divisor of \(p - 1\) and \(q - 1\), and so the same is true of \(j\). This shows that any common divisor \(j\) of \(\lambda(n)\) and the sum \((p - 1) + (q - 1)\) is also a common divisor of \(p - 1\) and \(q - 1\), and hence a divisor of \(\operatorname{GCD}(p - 1, q - 1)\).

Lemma 3: \(0 \le n - uv(p + q - 1) < n\)

Proof of Lemma 3:

contents.html:
It suffices to verify that \(0 < uv \le n/(p + q - 1)\). By the assumptions on the sizes of \(p\), \(q\), and \(n\), it follows that \(p + q - 1 < 2^{(\mathit{nBits}/2)+1}\) and \(n > 2^{(\mathit{nBits} - 1)}\), so that \(n/(p + q - 1) > 2^{(\mathit{nBits}/2) - 2}\). If it can be shown that the product \(uv\) is less than \(2^{(\mathit{nBits}/2) - 2}\), then the proof of Lemma 3 will be complete. Lemma 2 implies that \(1 \le uv \le u^2 < e^2\). By assumption, \(e < 2^{256}\), so \(e^2 < 2^{512}\). Since this document requires \(\mathit{nBits} \ge 2048\), it follows that \(2^{(\mathit{nBits}/2) - 2} \ge 2^{1022}\). The fact that \(uv < 2^{512} < 2^{1022} \le 2^{(\mathit{nBits}/2) - 2}\) completes the proof of the lemma.

Note: Lemma 3 (and hence the proof of correctness for the RecoverPrimeFactors process) is true under conditions more general than those used in the proof above, which invoked the bounds on the sizes of \(e\), \(p\), \(q\), and \(n\) that are required by this Recommendation. For example, it suffices to know that those four values satisfy the condition \(1 < e^2 \le n/(p + q - 1)\) and that \(d < \lambda(n)\).
contents.html_ja:
\(0 < uv \le n/(p + q - 1)\)を確認すれば十分である。\(p\)、\(q\)、\(n\)の大きさに関する仮定から、\(p + q - 1 < 2^{(\mathit{nBits}/2)+1}\)かつ\(n > 2^{(\mathit{nBits} - 1)}\)であり、したがって\(n/(p + q - 1) > 2^{(\mathit{nBits}/2) - 2}\)となる。積\(uv\)が\(2^{(\mathit{nBits}/2) - 2}\)より小さいことを示せば、補題3の証明は完了する。補題2から\(1 \le uv \le u^2 < e^2\)である。仮定により\(e < 2^{256}\)であるから、\(e^2 < 2^{512}\)である。本書は\(\mathit{nBits} \ge 2048\)を要求するので、\(2^{(\mathit{nBits}/2) - 2} \ge 2^{1022}\)となる。\(uv < 2^{512} < 2^{1022} \le 2^{(\mathit{nBits}/2) - 2}\)であることから、補題の証明が完了する。

注：補題3（したがってRecoverPrimeFactors手順の正しさの証明）は、上記の証明で用いた条件より一般的な条件の下でも成り立つ。上記の証明では、本勧告が要求する\(e\)、\(p\)、\(q\)、\(n\)の大きさの限界を用いた。例えば、これら四つの値が条件\(1 < e^2 \le n/(p + q - 1)\)を満たし、かつ\(d < \lambda(n)\)であることが分かれば十分である。

contents.html:
Now consider the quantities \(m\) and \(r\) computed in step 2 of the RecoverPrimeFactors process. Combining equation (5) with Lemma 3 yields

\[m = \lfloor a/n \rfloor = (uv - 1) \quad \text{and} \quad r = a - mn = n - uv(p + q - 1).\]

Therefore, in step 3 of the process,

\[b = ((n - r)/(m + 1)) + 1 = (uv(p + q - 1))/(uv)) + 1 = p + q,\]

and in step 4,

\[\Upsilon = (b^2 - 4n)^{1/2} = ((p + q)^2 - 4pq)^{1/2} = ((p - q)^2)^{1/2} = p - q.\]

These values for \(b\) and \(\Upsilon\) ensure that \(p\) and \(q\) are correctly recovered in step 5, since
contents.html_ja:
次に、RecoverPrimeFactors手順のステップ2で計算する量\(m\)と\(r\)を考える。式(5)と補題3を組み合わせると、次を得る。

\[m = \lfloor a/n \rfloor = (uv - 1) \quad \text{かつ} \quad r = a - mn = n - uv(p + q - 1).\]

したがって、手順のステップ3では

\[b = ((n - r)/(m + 1)) + 1 = (uv(p + q - 1))/(uv)) + 1 = p + q,\]

であり、ステップ4では

\[\Upsilon = (b^2 - 4n)^{1/2} = ((p + q)^2 - 4pq)^{1/2} = ((p - q)^2)^{1/2} = p - q.\]

となる。\(b\)と\(\Upsilon\)がこれらの値であれば、ステップ5で\(p\)と\(q\)が正しく復元される。なぜなら、次が成り立つからである。

contents.html: In the 2014 revision, the following revisions were made:
contents.html_ja: 2014年改訂では、次の改訂を行った。

contents.html: Section 3.1 – Added definitions of assumptions, binding, destroy, fresh, key-derivation function, key-derivation method, key-wrapping key, MAC tag, and trusted association; removed algorithm identifier, digital signature, initiator, responder.
contents.html_ja: 第3.1節 – 仮定、結合、破棄、新鮮、鍵導出関数、鍵導出方法、鍵ラッピング鍵、MACタグ、信頼された関連付けの定義を追加し、アルゴリズム識別子、デジタル署名、開始者、応答者を削除。

contents.html: Section 4 – Used party U and party V to name the parties, rather than using the initiator and responder as the parties. In Sections 8 and 9, the schemes have been accordingly renamed: KAS1-responder-confirmation is now KAS1-Party_V-confirmation, KAS2-responder-confirmation is now KAS2-Party_V-confirmation, KAS2-initiator-confirmation is now KAS2-Party_U-confirmation, KTS-OAEP-receiver-confirmation is not KTS-OAEP-Party_V-confirmation, and KTS-KEM-KWS-receiver-confirmation is now KTS-KEM-KWS-Party_V-confirmation.
contents.html_ja: 第4節 – 当事者の名称を開始者／応答者ではなく当事者U／当事者Vに変更。これに伴い、第8節および第9節のスキーム名を変更：KAS1-responder-confirmationをKAS1-Party_V-confirmationに、KAS2-responder-confirmationをKAS2-Party_V-confirmationに、KAS2-initiator-confirmationをKAS2-Party_U-confirmationに、KTS-OAEP-receiver-confirmationをKTS-OAEP-Party_V-confirmationに、KTS-KEM-KWS-receiver-confirmationをKTS-KEM-KWS-Party_V-confirmationに変更。

contents.html: Section 4 – Added requirements to destroy the local copies of secret and private values and all intermediate calculations before terminating a routine normally or in response to an error. Instructions to this effect have been inserted throughout the document.
contents.html_ja: 第4節 – 通常終了時またはエラー応答時にルーチンを終了する前に、秘密値・秘密鍵のローカルコピーとすべての中間計算値を破棄する要件を追加。この指示を文書全体に追加。

contents.html: The discussion about identifiers vs. identity and binding have been moved to Section 4.1.
contents.html_ja: 識別子とアイデンティティ、および結合に関する説明を第4.1節に移動。

contents.html: Section 4.3 – The phrase “IFC-based” has been removed throughout the document.
contents.html_ja: 第4.3節 – 文書全体から「IFC-based」という表現を削除。

contents.html: Section 5.4 – More discussion has been added about the use of nonces, including new requirements and recommendations.
contents.html_ja: 第5.4節 – 新たな要件および推奨事項を含め、ノンスの使用に関する説明を追加。

contents.html: Section 5.5 – Key derivation has been divided into single-step key derivation methods (Section 5.5.1), an extract-then-expand key derivation procedure (Section 5.5.2) and application-specific key-derivation methods (Section 5.5.3).

original_blocks.html:
Relatively primeTwo positive integers are relatively prime if their greatest common divisor is 1.
SchemeA set of unambiguously specified transformations that provide a (cryptographic) service when properly implemented and maintained. A scheme is a higher-level construct than a primitive and a lower- level construct than a protocol.
Security propertiesThe security features (e.g., replay protection, or key confirmation) that a cryptographic scheme may, or may not, provide.
Security strength (also, “Bits of security”)A number associated with the amount of work (that is, the number of operations) that is required to break a cryptographic algorithm or system.
SenderThe party that sends secret keying material to the receiver using a key-transport transaction. Contrast with receiver.
ShallThis term is used to indicate a requirement that needs to be fulfilled to claim conformance to this Recommendation. Note that shall may be coupled with not to become shall not.
Shared secretA secret value that has been computed during the execution of a key- establishment scheme, is known by both participants, and is used as input to a key-derivation method to produce secret keying material.
ShouldThis term is used to indicate an important recommendation. Ignoring the recommendation could result in undesirable results. Note that should may be coupled with not to become should not.
Support (a security strength)A security strength of s bits is said to be supported by a particular choice of algorithm, primitive, auxiliary function, parameters (etc.) for use in the implementation of a cryptographic mechanism if that choice will not prevent the resulting implementation from attaining a security strength of at least s bits. In this Recommendation, it is assumed that implementation choices are intended to support a security strength of 112 bits or more (see [SP 800-57]8 and [SP 800-131A]9).
original_blocks.html_ja:
Relatively prime2つの正整数の最大公約数が1であれば、互いに素である。
Scheme適切に実装・維持した場合に（暗号）サービスを提供する、曖昧さなく規定された変換の集合。スキームはプリミティブより高位で、プロトコルより低位の構成概念である。
Security properties暗号スキームが提供する場合としない場合のあるセキュリティ機能（再送防止や鍵確認など）。
Security strength（「セキュリティビット」ともいう）暗号アルゴリズムまたはシステムを破るために必要な作業量（演算回数）に対応する数値。

Shall本勧告への適合を主張するために満たす必要のある要件を示す語。shallにnotを組み合わせてshall notとする場合がある。

original_blocks.html: Each participant that is required to do so by the key-agreement scheme or the relying application/protocol obtains an identifier associated with the other entity, and verifies that the identifier of the other entity corresponds to the entity with whom the participant wishes to establish secret keying material. Each entity that requires the other entity’s public key for use in the key-agreement scheme obtains a public key that has a trusted association with the other party’s identifier, and obtains assurance of the validity of the public key. Approved methods for obtaining assurance of the validity of another entity’s public key are provided in Section 6.4.2. Each entity generates either a (random) secret value or a nonce, as required by the particular key-agreement scheme. If the scheme requires an entity to generate a secret value, that secret value is generated as specified in Section 5.3 and encrypted using the other entity's public key. The resulting ciphertext is then provided to the other entity. If the key-agreement scheme requires that an entity provide a nonce, that nonce is generated as specified in Section 5.4 and provided (in plaintext form) to the other party. (See Sections 8.2 and 8.3 for details). Each participant in the key-agreement process uses the appropriate public and/or private keys to establish a shared secret (Z) as specified in Section 8.2.2 or 8.3.2. Each participant then derives secret keying material from the shared secret (and other information), as specified in Section 5.5. If the key-agreement scheme includes key confirmation provided by one or both of the participants, then key confirmation is performed as specified in Section 8.2.3 or 8.3.3. When performed in accordance with those sections, successful key confirmation may also provide assurance that a key-pair owner possesses the (correct) private key (see Section 6.4.2.3.2). The owner of any key pair used during the key-agreement transaction is required to have assurance that the owner is in possession of the correct private key. Likewise, the recipient of another entity’s public key is required to have assurance that its owner is in possession of the corresponding private key. Assurance of private-key possession is obtained prior to using the derived keying material for purposes beyond those of the key-agreement transaction itself. This assurance may be provided/obtained either through key confirmation, or by some other approved means (see Sections 6.4.1 and 6.4.2).
original_blocks.html_ja: 鍵合意スキームまたは利用アプリケーション／プロトコルが求める各参加者は、他方の主体に関連付けられた識別子を取得し、その識別子が秘密鍵素材を確立しようとする相手主体に対応することを検証する。鍵合意スキームで他方の主体の公開鍵を必要とする各主体は、相手の識別子と信頼できる形で関連付けられた公開鍵を取得し、その公開鍵の妥当性の保証を取得する。他の主体の公開鍵の妥当性の保証を得る承認済み方法は第6.4.2節に示す。各主体は、個々の鍵合意スキームが求めるとおり、（ランダムな）秘密値またはノンスを生成する。スキームが秘密値の生成を求める場合は、第5.3節に従って秘密値を生成し、他方の主体の公開鍵で暗号化する。生成した暗号文を他方の主体に渡す。スキームがノンスの提供を求める場合は、第5.4節に従ってノンスを生成し、平文のまま相手に渡す（詳細は第8.2節および第8.3節参照）。鍵合意プロセスの各参加者は、第8.2.2節または第8.3.2節に従って、適切な公開鍵および／または秘密鍵を使い共有秘密（Z）を確立する。続いて各参加者は、第5.5節に従い、共有秘密（および他の情報）から秘密鍵素材を導出する。鍵合意スキームに一方または両方の参加者が行う鍵確認が含まれる場合、第8.2.3節または第8.3.3節に従って鍵確認を行う。これらの節に従って実施した場合、鍵確認の成功は、鍵ペアの所有者が正しい秘密鍵を所持する保証も与え得る（第6.4.2.3.2節参照）。鍵合意トランザクション中に使用する鍵ペアの所有者は、正しい秘密鍵を所持している保証を得る必要がある。同様に、他の主体の公開鍵を受領した主体は、その所有者が対応する秘密鍵を所持している保証を得る必要がある。導出鍵素材を鍵合意トランザクション自体の目的以外に使用する前に、秘密鍵所持の保証を取得する。この保証は鍵確認または他の承認済み手段で提供／取得してよい（第6.4.1節および第6.4.2節参照）。

The input to a MAC function includes a symmetric key, called MacKey, and a binary data string, called MacData. A MAC function is represented as MAC(MacKey, MacData {, ...})12. In this Recommendation, a MAC function is used in key confirmation (see Section 5.6) and may be used for key derivation (see Section 5.5 and SP 800-
original_blocks.html_ja: メッセージ認証コード（MAC）アルゴリズムは、対称鍵をパラメータとする一方向（MAC）関数の族を定める。MAC関数への入力には、MacKeyと呼ぶ対称鍵と、MacDataと呼ぶ2進データ文字列が含まれる。MAC関数を MAC(MacKey, MacData {, ...})¹² と表す。本勧告ではMAC関数を鍵確認に用い（第5.6節参照）、鍵導出にも使用できる（第5.5節およびSP 800-

original_blocks.html: It must be computationally infeasible to determine the MAC of a (newly formed) MacData value without knowledge of the MacKey value (even if one has seen the MACs corresponding to other MacData values that were computed using that same MacKey value). Key confirmation requires the use of one of the following approved MAC algorithms: HMAC, AES-CMAC or KMAC. HMAC is specified in FIPS 198 and requires the use of an approved hash function. AES-CMAC is specified in SP 800-38B13 for the AES block cipher algorithm specified in FIPS 197. KMAC is specified in SP 800-185.14 When used for key confirmation, the key-confirmation provider is required to compute a "MAC tag" on received or derived data using the agreed-upon MAC function. A symmetric key derived from a shared secret (during a key-agreement transaction) or extracted from transported keying material (during a key-transport transaction) is used as MacKey. The resulting MAC tag is sent to the key-confirmation recipient, who can obtain assurance (via MAC-tag verification) that the shared secret and derived keying material were correctly computed (in the case of key agreement) or that the transported keying material was successfully received (in the case of key transport). MAC-tag computation and verification are defined in Sections 5.2.1 and 5.2.2.

original_blocks.html: To verify the MAC tag received during key confirmation, a new MAC tag, MacTag′, is computed as specified in Section 5.2.1 using the values of MacKey, MacTagBits, and MacData possessed by the key-confirmation recipient. MacTag′is compared with the received MAC tag (i.e., MacTag). If their values are equal, then it may be inferred that the same MacKey, MacTagBits, and MacData values were used in the computation of MacTag and MacTag′. That is, successful verification provides evidence that the key-confirmation provider has obtained the same MAC key as the key-confirmation recipient.
original_blocks.html_ja: 鍵確認中に受信したMACタグを検証するため、鍵確認受領者が持つMacKey、MacTagBitsおよびMacDataを用い、第5.2.1節に従って新たなMACタグMacTag′を計算する。MacTag′を受信したMACタグ（すなわちMacTag）と比較する。値が等しい場合、MacTagとMacTag′の計算に同じMacKey、MacTagBitsおよびMacData値が用いられたと推定できる。つまり、検証の成功は、鍵確認提供者が鍵確認受領者と同じMAC鍵を得たことの証拠となる。

original_blocks.html: When an approved RBG is used to generate a secret value as part of a key-establishment scheme specified in this Recommendation (e.g., Z in a scheme from the KAS1 family), that RBG shall be instantiated to support a security strength that is equal to or greater than the security strength associated with the RSA modulus length as specified in SP 800-57, Part 1.

original_blocks.html: A nonce is a time-varying value that has a negligible chance of repeating (where the meaning of “negligible” may be application specific). original_blocks.html: For the KAS1 schemes, the required nonce N should be a random nonce containing a random bit V string output from an approved random bit generator (RBG), where both the security strength supported by the instantiation of the random bit generator and the bit length of the random bit string are greater than or equal to the targeted security strength of the key-agreement scheme in which the nonce is used; when feasible, the bit length of the random bit string should be (at least) twice the targeted security strength. For details concerning the security strength supported by an instantiation of a random bit generator, see SP 800-90. As part of the proper implementation of this Recommendation, system users and/or agents trusted to act on their behalf should determine that the components selected for inclusion in required nonces meet the security requirements of those users or agents. The application tasked with performing key establishment on behalf of a party should determine whether or not to proceed with a key-establishment transaction, based upon the perceived adequacy of the method(s) used to form the required nonces. Such knowledge may be explicitly provided to the application in some manner, or may be implicitly provided by the operation of the application itself.
original_blocks.html_ja: KAS1スキームでは、必須ノンスN_Vは承認済み乱数ビット生成器（RBG）が出力するランダムビット文字列を含むランダムノンスであるべきである。RBGのインスタンス化がサポートするセキュリティ強度とランダムビット文字列のビット長は、いずれもそのノンスを使う鍵合意スキームの目標セキュリティ強度以上でなければならない。実行可能な場合、ランダムビット文字列の長さは目標セキュリティ強度の少なくとも2倍とするべきである。RBGのインスタンス化がサポートするセキュリティ強度の詳細はSP 800-90を参照。適切に本勧告を実装するため、システム利用者および／またはその代理として行動することを信頼された者は、必須ノンスに含める要素が自身のセキュリティ要件を満たすことを判断するべきである。主体に代わって鍵確立を行うアプリケーションは、必須ノンスの生成方法が十分であるとの判断に基づき、鍵確立トランザクションを進めるかどうかを決定するべきである。そのような情報は何らかの方法でアプリケーションに明示的に提供されてもよく、アプリケーション自体の動作を通じて暗黙的に提供されてもよい。

original_blocks.html: An approved key-derivation method shall be used to derive keying material from the shared secret Z during the execution of a key-establishment scheme from the KAS1 or KAS2 family of schemes. The shared secret shall be used only by an approved key-derivation method and shall not be used for any other purpose.
original_blocks.html_ja: KAS1またはKAS2ファミリーの鍵確立スキームの実行中、共有秘密Zから鍵素材を導出するには承認済み鍵導出方法を使用しなければならない。共有秘密は承認済み鍵導出方法だけで使用し、他の目的に使用してはならない。

original_blocks.html: When employed during the execution of a key-establishment scheme as specified in this Recommendation, the agreed-upon key-derivation method uses input that includes a freshly created shared secret Z along with other information. The derived keying material shall be computed in its entirety before outputting any portion of it, and (all copies of) Z shall be treated as a critical security parameter (in a cryptographic module that is compliant with FIPS 140) and destroyed immediately following its use. The output produced by a key-derivation method using input that includes the shared secret created during the execution of any key-establishment scheme specified in this Recommendation shall only be used as secret keying material – such as a symmetric key used for data encryption or message integrity, a secret initialization vector, or, perhaps, a key-derivation key that will be used to generate additional keying material (possibly using a different process – see SP 800-10816). The derived keying material shall not be used as a key stream for a stream cipher. Non-secret keying material (such as a non-secret initialization vector) shall not be generated using a key-derivation method that includes the shared secret, Z, as input (this restriction applies to all one-step and two-step key-derivation methods in SP 800-56C).
original_blocks.html_ja: 本勧告で規定する鍵確立スキームの実行時には、合意済み鍵導出方法は、新たに生成した共有秘密Zと他の情報を含む入力を使用する。導出鍵素材はその一部を出力する前に全体を計算しなければならず、Z（およびそのすべてのコピー）は、FIPS 140準拠暗号モジュールでは重要セキュリティパラメータとして扱い、使用後直ちに破棄しなければならない。本勧告の鍵確立スキームの実行中に生成した共有秘密を入力に含む鍵導出方法の出力は、データ暗号化またはメッセージ完全性に用いる対称鍵、秘密初期化ベクトル、あるいは追加鍵素材を生成する鍵導出鍵（別のプロセスを使う場合もある。SP 800-108¹⁶参照）など、秘密鍵素材としてのみ使用しなければならない。導出鍵素材をストリーム暗号の鍵ストリームとして使用してはならない。非秘密鍵素材（非秘密初期化ベクトルなど）を、共有秘密Zを入力に含む鍵導出方法で生成してはならない（この制限はSP 800-56Cのすべての一段階および二段階鍵導出方法に適用される）。

original_blocks.html_ja: Zは共有秘密を表すバイト文字列、

original_blocks.html_ja: salt：バイト文字列、

original_blocks.html: The bit string FixedInfo should be used to ensure that the derived keying material is adequately “bound” to the context of the key-establishment transaction. Although other methods may be used to bind keying material to the transaction context, this Recommendation makes no statement as to the adequacy of these other methods. original_blocks.html: Context-specific information that may be appropriate for inclusion in FixedInfo includes the following:
original_blocks.html_ja: FixedInfoに含めるのが適切なコンテキスト固有情報には、次のものがある。

original_blocks.html: For rationale in support of including entity identifiers, scheme identifiers, and/or other information in OtherInput, see Appendix B of SP 800-56A. When FixedInfo is used, the meaning of each information item and each item’s position within the FixedInfo bit string shall be specified. In addition, each item of information included in FixedInfo shall be unambiguously represented. For example, each item of information could take the form of a fixed-length bit string, or, if greater flexibility is needed, an item of information could be represented in a Datalen || Data format, where Data is a variable-length string of zero or more (eight-bit) bytes, and Datalen is a fixed-length, big-endian counter that indicates the byte length of Data. These requirements can be satisfied, for example, by using ASN.1 DER encoding as specified in Section 5.5.2.1.2.
original_blocks.html_ja: OtherInputに主体識別子、スキーム識別子および／またはその他の情報を含める根拠は、SP 800-56Aの付録Bを参照。FixedInfoを用いる場合、各情報項目の意味とFixedInfoビット列内の位置を規定しなければならない。また、FixedInfoに含める各情報項目は曖昧さなく表現しなければならない。例えば、各情報項目を固定長ビット列とするか、柔軟性を高める必要がある場合はDatalen || Data形式で表現できる。ここでDataは0個以上の8ビットバイトからなる可変長文字列、DatalenはDataのバイト長を示す固定長ビッグエンディアンカウンタである。これらの要件は、例えば第5.5.2.1.2節に規定するASN.1 DERエンコードによって満たせる。

One of those two formats should be used by a one-step key-derivation method specified in SP 800-56C when the auxiliary function employed is H = hash.

original_blocks.html: When FixedInfo is included during the key-derivation process, and the recommended formats are used, the included items of information shall be divided into (three, four, or five) subfields as defined below. AlgorithmID: A required non-null subfield that indicates how the derived keying material will be parsed and for which algorithm(s) the derived secret keying material will be used. For example, AlgorithmID might indicate that bits 1 to 112 are to be used as a 112-bit HMAC key and that bits 113 to 240 are to be used as a 128-bit AES key. PartyUInfo: A required non-null subfield containing public information about party U. At a minimum, PartyUInfo shall include ID , an identifier for party U, as a distinct item of U information. This subfield could also include information about the public key (if any) contributed to the key-establishment transaction by party U. Although the schemes specified in the Recommendation do not require the contribution of a nonce by party U, any nonce provided by party U should be included in this subfield. PartyVInfo: A required non-null subfield containing public information about party V. At a minimum, PartyVInfo shall include ID , an identifier for party V, as a distinct item of V information. This subfield could also include information about the public key contributed to the key-establishment transaction by party V. When the key-derivation method is used in a KAS1 scheme (see Section 8.2), the nonce, N supplied by party V shall be included in this V, field. SuppPubInfo: An optional subfield that contains additional, mutually known public information (e.g., L, an identifier for the particular key-establishment scheme that was used to determine Z, an indication of the protocol or application employing that scheme, a session identifier, etc.; this is particularly useful if these aspects of the key-establishment transaction can vary). While an implementation may be capable of including this subfield, the subfield may be Null for a given transaction. SuppPrivInfo: An optional subfield that contains additional, mutually known private information (e.g., a secret symmetric key that has been communicated through a separate channel). While an implementation may be capable of including this subfield, the subfield may be Null for a given transaction.
original_blocks.html_ja: 鍵導出プロセスでFixedInfoを含め、推奨形式を用いる場合、含める情報項目は以下の3、4または5個のサブフィールドに分けなければならない。AlgorithmID：導出鍵素材の解析方法と、導出された秘密鍵素材を使用するアルゴリズムを示す、必須かつ空でないサブフィールド。例えば、ビット1～112を112ビットHMAC鍵、ビット113～240を128ビットAES鍵として使用することを示せる。PartyUInfo：当事者Uの公開情報を含む必須かつ空でないサブフィールド。最低限、ID_U（当事者Uの識別子）を独立した情報項目として含めなければならない。当事者Uが鍵確立トランザクションに提供した公開鍵（ある場合）の情報も含めてよい。本勧告のスキームは当事者Uによるノンス提供を要求しないが、Uがノンスを提供した場合は本サブフィールドに含めるべきである。PartyVInfo：当事者Vの公開情報を含む必須かつ空でないサブフィールド。最低限、ID_V（当事者Vの識別子）を独立した情報項目として含めなければならない。当事者Vがトランザクションに提供した公開鍵情報も含めてよい。KAS1スキーム（第8.2節参照）で鍵導出方法を使う場合、当事者Vが供給するノンスN_Vを本フィールドに含めなければならない。SuppPubInfo：追加の、相互に既知の公開情報（L、Zの決定に使った特定の鍵確立スキームの識別子、そのスキームを使うプロトコルまたはアプリケーションの識別情報、セッション識別子など）を含む任意のサブフィールド。鍵確立トランザクションの条件が変化し得る場合に特に有用である。実装はこのサブフィールドを含める機能を備えてもよいが、特定のトランザクションではNullでもよい。SuppPrivInfo：追加の、相互に既知の秘密情報（別経路で伝達した秘密対称鍵など）を含む任意のサブフィールド。実装は本サブフィールドを含める機能を備えてもよいが、特定のトランザクションではNullでもよい。

original_blocks.html: 5.5.2.1.1 The Concatenation Format for FixedInfo
original_blocks.html_ja: 5.5.2.1.1 FixedInfoの連結形式

original_blocks.html: This section specifies the concatenation format for FixedInfo. This format has been designed to provide a simple means of binding the derived keying material to the context of the key-establishment transaction, independent of other actions taken by the relying application. Note: When the one-step key-derivation method specified in SP 800-56C is used with H = hash as the auxiliary function and this concatenation format for FixedInfo, the resulting key-derivation method is the Concatenation Key-Derivation Function specified in the original version of SP 800-56A. For this format, FixedInfo is a bit string equal to the following concatenation: AlgorithmID || PartyUInfo || PartyVInfo {|| SuppPubInfo }{|| SuppPrivInfo }, where the five subfields are bit strings comprised of items of information as described in Section 5.5.2.1.
original_blocks.html_ja: 本節ではFixedInfoの連結形式を規定する。この形式は、利用アプリケーション側で行う他の処理とは独立して、導出鍵素材を鍵確立トランザクションのコンテキストに結び付ける簡単な方法を提供するよう設計されている。注：補助関数H = hashを用いるSP 800-56Cの一段階鍵導出方法でこのFixedInfo連結形式を使うと、旧版SP 800-56Aに規定された連結鍵導出関数となる。この形式では、FixedInfoは次の連結に等しいビット列である：AlgorithmID || PartyUInfo || PartyVInfo {|| SuppPubInfo }{|| SuppPrivInfo }。5つのサブフィールドは、第5.5.2.1節で説明した情報項目から構成するビット列である。

original_blocks.html: Each of the three required subfields AlgorithmID, PartyUInfo, and PartyVInfo shall be the concatenation of a pre-determined sequence of substrings in which each substring represents a distinct item of information. Each such substring shall have one of these two formats: either it is a fixed-length bit string, or it has the form Datalen || Data – where Data is a variable-length string of zero or more (eight-bit) bytes, and Datalen is a fixed-length, big-endian counter that indicates the byte length of Data. (In this variable-length format, a null string of data shall be represented by a zero value for Datalen, indicating the absence of following data.) A protocol using this format for FixedInfo shall specify the number, ordering and meaning of the information-bearing substrings that are included in each of the subfields (i.e., AlgorithmID, PartyUInfo, and PartyVInfo), and shall also specify which of the two formats (fixed-length or variable-length) is used by each such substring to represent its distinct item of information. The protocol shall specify the lengths for all fixed-length quantities, including the Datalen counters. Each of the optional SuppPrivInfo and SuppPubInfo subfields (when allowed by the protocol employing the one-step key-derivation method) shall be the concatenation of a pre-determined sequence of substrings representing additional items of information that may be used during key derivation upon mutual agreement of parties U and V. Each substring representing an item of information shall be of the form Datalen || Data, where Data is a variable-length string of zero or more (eight-bit) bytes, and Datalen is a fixed-length, big-endian counter that indicates the byte length of Data; the use of this form for the information allows U and V to omit a particular information item without confusion about the meaning of the other information that is provided in the SuppPrivInfo or SuppPubInfo subfield. The substrings representing items of information that parties U and V choose not to contribute are set equal to Null, and are represented in this variable-length format by setting Datalen equal to zero. If a protocol allows the use of the FixedInfo subfield SuppPrivInfo and/or the subfield SuppPubInfo, then the protocol shall specify the number, ordering and meaning of additional items of information that may be used in the allowed subfield(s) and shall specify the fixed-length of the Datalen counters.

original_blocks.html: The ASN.1 format for FixedInfo provides an alternative means of binding the derived keying material to the context of the key-establishment transaction, independent of other actions taken by the relying application. Note: When the one-step key-derivation method specified in SP 800-56C is used with H = hash as the auxiliary function and with this ASN.1 format for FixedInfo, the resulting key-derivation method is the ASN.1 Key-Derivation Function specified in the original version of SP 800-56B. For the ASN.1 format, FixedInfo is a bit string resulting from the ASN.1 Distinguished Encoding Rules (DER) encoding (see ISO/IEC 8825-1) of a data structure comprised of a sequence of three required subfields AlgorithmID, PartyUInfo, and PartyVInfo, and, optionally, a subfield SuppPubInfo and/or a subfield SuppPrivInfo – as described in Section 5.5.2.1. original_blocks.html: As specified in this Recommendation, unilateral key confirmation occurs when one participant in the execution of a key-establishment scheme (the key-confirmation “provider”) demonstrates to the satisfaction of the other participant (the key-confirmation “recipient”) that both the KC provider and the KC recipient have possession of the same secret MacKey. MacKey shall be a symmetric key that is unique to a specific execution of a key-establishment scheme and (from the perspective of the KC provider) shall be unpredictable prior to that key-establishment transaction. In the case of a key-agreement scheme, MacKey is derived using the shared secret Z created during the execution of that scheme (see Section 5.5 for the details of key derivation). In the case of a key-transport scheme, MacKey is included as part of the transported keying material. Step_2 below specifies how MacKey is to be extracted from the derived or transported keying material. MacKey and certain context-specific MacData (as specified below) are used by the KC provider as input to an approved MAC algorithm to obtain a MAC tag that is sent to the KC recipient. The recipient performs an independent computation of the MAC tag. If the MAC tag value computed by the KC recipient matches the MAC tag value received from the KC provider, then key confirmation is successful. (See Section 5.2 for MAC-tag generation and verification, and Section 5.6.3 for a discussion of MAC-tag security.) In the case of a scheme providing key-agreement, successful key confirmation following key agreement provides assurance to the KC recipient that the same Z value has been used by both parties to correctly derive the keying material (which includes MacKey). In the case of a key-transport scheme (see Section 9.2.4), successful key confirmation provides assurance to the KC recipient (who sent the keying material) that the transported keying material (which includes MacKey) has been correctly decrypted by the party to whom it was sent. A close examination of the KC process shows that each of the pair-wise key-establishment schemes specified in this Recommendation that incorporate key confirmation can be used to provide the KC recipient with assurance that the KC provider is currently in possession of the (correct) private key – the one corresponding to the KC provider’s public key-establishment key. The use of transaction-specific values for both MacKey and MacData prevents (for all practical purposes) the replay of any previously computed value of MacTag. The receipt of a correctly computed MAC tag provides assurance to the KC recipient that the KC provider has used the correct private key during the current transaction – to successfully recover the secret data that is a prerequisite to learning the value of MacKey. To include unilateral key confirmation, the following steps shall be incorporated into the scheme. (Additional details will be provided for each scheme in the appropriate subsections of Sections 8 and 9.) In the discussion that follows, the key-confirmation provider, P, may be either party U or party V, as long as the KC provider, P, contributes a key pair to the key-establishment transaction. The key-confirmation recipient, R, is the other party.

original_blocks.html: A valid RSA key pair, in its basic form, shall consist of an RSA public key (n, e) and an RSA private key (n, d), where:
original_blocks.html_ja: 有効な基本形式のRSA鍵ペアは、RSA公開鍵(n, e)およびRSA秘密鍵(n, d)で構成しなければならない。ここで：

original_blocks.html: n, the public modulus, shall be the product of exactly two distinct, odd positive prime factors, p and q, that are kept secret. Let len(n) = nBits, the bit length of n; len(n) is required to be even.
original_blocks.html_ja: n（公開法）は、互いに異なる2つの奇正素数pおよびqの積でなければならず、pとqは秘密に保持する。len(n) = nBitsとし、nのビット長len(n)は偶数でなければならない。

original_blocks.html: The public exponent e shall be an odd integer that is selected prior to the generation of p and q such that: 65,537 ≤ e < 2256
original_blocks.html_ja: 公開指数eは奇整数でなければならず、pおよびqの生成前に選択し、65,537 ≤ e < 2^256を満たす。

original_blocks.html: The prime factors p and q shall be generated using one of the methods specified in Appendix B.3 of FIPS 186 such that: a. 2(nBits − 1)/2 < p < 2nBits/2. b. 2(nBits − 1)/2 < q < 2nBits/2. c. |p – q| > 2nBits/2−100.
original_blocks.html_ja: 素因数pおよびqはFIPS 186付録B.3のいずれかの方法で生成し、次を満たさなければならない。a. 2^((nBits−1)/2) < p < 2^(nBits/2)。b. 2^((nBits−1)/2) < q < 2^(nBits/2)。c. |p − q| > 2^(nBits/2−100)。

original_blocks.html: d. The exponent e must be mutually prime with both p − 1 and q − 1: GCD(e, LCM(p − 1, q − 1)) = 1.
original_blocks.html_ja: d. 指数eはp − 1およびq − 1の両方と互いに素でなければならない：GCD(e, LCM(p − 1, q − 1)) = 1。

original_blocks.html: The primes p and q, and the private exponent d shall be selected such that: a. 2nBits/2 < d < LCM(p−1, q−1), and b. d = e−1 mod (LCM(p−1, q−1)). Regarding step 4a: One can be certain that the inequality 2nBits/2 < d will be satisfied even before d is computed by verifying that LCM(p−1, q−1) ≥ (e)( 2nBits/2 ). The second inequality, d < LCM(p−1, q−1), will be satisfied if d is computed as specified in step b).
original_blocks.html_ja: 素数pとq、および秘密指数dは次を満たすよう選択しなければならない。a. 2^(nBits/2) < d < LCM(p−1, q−1)。b. d = e⁻¹ mod LCM(p−1, q−1)。手順4aについて：dを計算する前でも、LCM(p−1, q−1) ≥ e × 2^(nBits/2)を検証すれば、2^(nBits/2) < dの不等式が成立すると確認できる。2つ目の不等式d < LCM(p−1, q−1)は、手順bのとおりdを計算すれば成立する。

original_blocks.html: The RSA private key may be expressed in several formats. The basic format of the RSA private key consists of the modulus n and a private-key exponent d that depends on n and the public-key exponent e; this format is used to specify the RSA primitives and operations in Section 7. The other two formats may be used in implementations, but may require appropriate modifications for correct implementation. To facilitate implementation testing, the format for the private key shall be one of the following:
original_blocks.html_ja: RSA秘密鍵は複数の形式で表現できる。基本形式は、法nと、nおよび公開指数eに依存する秘密指数dから成る。この形式は第7節のRSAプリミティブおよび操作を規定するために用いる。他の2形式も実装で使用できるが、正しく実装するには適切な変更が必要となる場合がある。実装試験を容易にするため、秘密鍵は次のいずれかの形式でなければならない。

original_blocks.html: The basic format: (n, d).
original_blocks.html_ja: 基本形式：(n, d)。

original_blocks.html: The prime-factor format: (p, q, d).
original_blocks.html_ja: 素因数形式：(p, q, d)。

original_blocks.html: The Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) format: (n, e, d, p, q, dP, dQ, qInv), where dP = d mod (p – 1), dQ = d mod (q – 1), and qInv = q–1 mod p. Note that Section 7.1.2 discusses the use of the private key expressed using the CRT format during the execution of the RSA decryption primitive.
original_blocks.html_ja: 中国剰余定理（CRT）形式：(n, e, d, p, q, dP, dQ, qInv)。ここでdP = d mod (p−1)、dQ = d mod (q−1)、qInv = q⁻¹ mod pである。第7.1.2節では、RSA復号プリミティブの実行中にCRT形式の秘密鍵を用いることを説明する。

original_blocks.html: The key pairs employed by the key-establishment schemes specified in this Recommendation shall be generated using the techniques specified in Appendix B.3 of FIPS 186, employing the requisite methods for prime-number generation, primality testing, etc., that are specified in Appendix C of that document. Note that these generation methods ensure that the prime factors p and q have the same bit length and that their product, n (the RSA modulus), has a bit length that is exactly twice the length of its factors. An approved RSA key-pair generator and approved random bit generator (RBG) shall be used to produce an RSA key pair. Any modulus with an even bit length that provides at least 112 bits of security strength may be used. Commonly used modulus lengths and their associated security strengths are given in Table 2. For other modulus lengths, Appendix D provides a method for estimating the security strength that can be supported. Table 2: Security Strengths Supported by Commonly Used Modulus Lengths17

original_blocks.html: A routine that implements this generation function shall destroy any local copies of p, q, and d, as well as any other locally stored values used or produced during the execution of the routine. The destruction of these locally stored values shall occur prior to or during any exit from the routine (whether exiting early because of an error, or exiting normally with the output of an RSA key pair). Note that the requirement for destruction includes any locally stored portions of the output key pair.

original_blocks.html: RSA-OAEP consists of asymmetric encryption and decryption operations that are based on an approved hash function, an approved random bit generator, a mask-generation function, and the RSAEP and RSADP primitives. These operations are used by the KTS-OAEP key-transport scheme (see Section 9.2). In the RSA-OAEP encryption operation, a data block is constructed by the sender (party U) from the keying material to be transported and the hash of additional input (see Section 9.1) that is shared by party U and the intended receiving party (party V). A random byte string is generated, after which both the random byte string and the data block are masked in a way that binds their values. The masked values are used to form the plaintext that is input to the RSAEP primitive, along with the public key-establishment key of party V. The resulting RSAEP output further binds the random byte string, the keying material and the hash of the additional data in the ciphertext that is sent to party V. In the RSA-OAEP decryption operation, the ciphertext and the receiving party’s (i.e., party V’s) private key-establishment key are input to the RSADP primitive, recovering the masked values as output. The mask-generation function is then used to reconstruct and remove the masks that obscure the random byte string and the data block. After removing the masks, party V can examine the format of the recovered data and compare its own computation of the hash of the additional data to the hash value contained in the unmasked data block, thus obtaining some measure of assurance of the integrity of the recovered data – including the transported keying material. RSA-OAEP can process up to nLen – 2HLen – 2 bytes of keying material, where nLen is the byte length of the recipient’s RSA modulus, and HLen is the byte length of the values output by the underlying hash function.
original_blocks.html_ja: RSA-OAEPは、承認済みハッシュ関数、承認済み乱数ビット生成器、マスク生成関数、およびRSAEP／RSADPプリミティブに基づく非対称暗号化・復号操作から成る。これらの操作はKTS-OAEP鍵転送スキームで用いる（第9.2節参照）。RSA-OAEP暗号化操作では、送信者（当事者U）が転送対象の鍵素材と、Uおよび意図する受信者（当事者V）が共有する追加入力（第9.1節参照）のハッシュからデータブロックを構成する。ランダムバイト文字列を生成した後、そのランダム文字列とデータブロックの値を結び付ける方法で双方をマスクする。マスク済み値から平文を構成し、当事者Vの公開鍵確立鍵とともにRSAEPプリミティブへ入力する。RSAEP出力により、ランダム文字列、鍵素材および追加入力のハッシュがさらに結び付けられ、当事者Vに送る暗号文となる。RSA-OAEP復号操作では、暗号文と受信者（当事者V）の秘密鍵確立鍵をRSADPプリミティブへ入力し、マスク済み値を出力として復元する。続いてマスク生成関数で、ランダムバイト文字列とデータブロックを隠すマスクを再構成して除去する。マスク除去後、当事者Vは復元データの形式を検査し、追加入力のハッシュを自ら計算した値と、マスク解除済みデータブロックに含まれるハッシュ値を比較できる。これにより、転送鍵素材を含む復元データの完全性について一定の保証を得る。RSA-OAEPは最大nLen − 2HLen − 2バイトの鍵素材を処理できる。nLenは受信者のRSA法のバイト長、HLenは基礎ハッシュ関数が出力する値のバイト長である。

original_blocks.html: In a key-agreement scheme, two parties, party U and party V, establish keying material over which neither has complete control of the result, but both have influence. This Recommendation provides two families of key-agreement schemes: KAS1 and KAS2. The KAS1 family consists of the KAS1-basic and KAS1-Party_V-confirmation schemes, and the KAS2 family consists of the KAS2-basic, KAS2-Party_V-confirmation, KAS2-Party_U-confirmation, and KAS2-bilateral-confirmation schemes. These schemes are based on secret-value encapsulation (see Section 7.2.1). Key confirmation is included in some of these schemes to provide assurance that the participants share the same keying material; see Section 5.6 for the details of key confirmation. When possible, each party should have such assurance. Although other methods are often used to provide this assurance, this Recommendation makes no statement as to the adequacy of these other methods. Key confirmation may also provide assurance of private-key possession. For each of the KAS1 and KAS2 schemes, Party V shall have an identifier, ID , that has an

original_blocks.html: Party U and/or party V may additionally provide key confirmation. If key confirmation is incorporated, then the derived keying material is parsed into two parts, MacKey and KeyData. MacKey is then used to compute a MAC tag of MacTagLen bytes on MacData (see Sections 5.2.1, 5.2.2, 5.6.1 and 5.6.3). Key confirmation may be either unilateral or bilateral. When key confirmation is performed, a MacTag is sent from a KC provider to a KC recipient.
original_blocks.html_ja: 当事者Uおよび／またはVはさらに鍵確認を提供してもよい。鍵確認を組み込む場合、導出鍵素材をMacKeyとKeyDataの2つの部分に解析する。次に、MacKeyを用いてMacDataに対するMacTagLenバイトのMACタグを計算する（第5.2.1節、第5.2.2節、第5.6.1節および第5.6.3節参照）。鍵確認は一方向でも双方向でもよい。鍵確認を実施する場合、KC提供者からKC受領者にMacTagを送る。

original_blocks.html: Additional input to the key-transport process may be employed to ensure that the keying material is adequately “bound” to the context of the key-transport transaction. The use of additional input, A, is explicitly supported by the key-transport schemes specified in Section 9.2. Each party to a key-transport transaction shall know whether or not additional input is employed in that transaction. Context-specific information that may be appropriate for inclusion in the additional input is listed in Section 5.5.2. (The suggestions for the content of FixedfInfo apply to the additional input as well.) Both parties to the key-transport transaction shall know the format of the additional input, A, and shall acquire A in time to use it as required by the scheme. The methods used for formatting and distributing the additional input are application-defined. System users and/or agents trusted to act on their behalf should determine that the information selected for inclusion in A and the methods used for formatting and distributing A meet the security requirements of those users.
original_blocks.html_ja: 鍵転送プロセスでは、鍵素材を鍵転送トランザクションのコンテキストに適切に「結び付ける」ため、追加入力を使用してもよい。第9.2節の鍵転送スキームは追加入力Aを明示的にサポートする。鍵転送トランザクションの各当事者は、そのトランザクションで追加入力を用いるか否かを把握していなければならない。追加入力に含めるのが適切なコンテキスト固有情報を第5.5.2節に列挙する（FixedInfoの内容に関する提案は追加入力にも適用される）。両当事者は追加入力Aの形式を知り、スキームの要求に応じて利用できるよう適時にAを取得しなければならない。追加入力の形式設定および配布方法はアプリケーションで定義する。システム利用者および／または信頼された代理人は、Aに含める情報とAの形式設定・配布方法がセキュリティ要件を満たすと判断するべきである。

original_blocks.html: If key confirmation is incorporated, then the transported keying material is parsed into two parts, a transaction-specific (random) value for MacKey, followed by KeyData (see Section 5.6.1). The Mackey portion of the keying material and an approved MAC algorithm are used by each party to compute a MAC tag (of an appropriate, agreed-upon length) on what should be the same MacData (see Sections 5.6 and 9.2.4.2). The MAC tag computed by party V (the key-confirmation provider) is sent to party U (the key-confirmation recipient). If the value of the MAC tag sent by party V matches the MAC tag value computed by party U, then party U obtains a confirmation of the success of the key-transport transaction.
original_blocks.html_ja: 鍵確認を組み込む場合、転送鍵素材をトランザクション固有のランダム値MacKeyと、その後に続くKeyDataの2部分に解析する（第5.6.1節参照）。双方の当事者は鍵素材のMacKey部分と承認済みMACアルゴリズムを用い、同一であるべきMacDataに対するMACタグを合意済みの適切な長さで計算する（第5.6節および第9.2.4.2節参照）。当事者V（鍵確認提供者）が計算したMACタグを当事者U（鍵確認受領者）に送る。VのMACタグ値とUが計算した値が一致すれば、Uは鍵転送トランザクションの成功を確認する。

original_blocks.html: Each KTS-OAEP scheme requires Alice to employ the RSA-OAEP.ENCRYPT operation to encrypt the selected keying material (and any additional input) as ciphertext C, using Bob’s RSA public key. Unless Bob’s corresponding private key has been compromised, Alice has assurance that no unintended entity (i.e., no one but Bob) could employ the RSA-OAEP.DECRYPT operation to obtain the transported keying material from C. Absent the compromise of Bob’s RSA private key (or some compromise of the keying material itself – perhaps prior to transport), Alice may attain a certain level of confidence that she has correctly identified party V as Bob. Alice’s level of confidence is commensurate with:
original_blocks.html_ja: 各KTS-OAEPスキームでAliceはRSA-OAEP.ENCRYPT操作を用い、選択した鍵素材（および追加入力があればそれも）をBobのRSA公開鍵で暗号化して暗号文Cにする。Bobの対応秘密鍵が侵害されていなければ、Bob以外の意図しない主体がRSA-OAEP.DECRYPTによりCから転送鍵素材を得ることはできないとAliceは保証される。BobのRSA秘密鍵または鍵素材自体（転送前など）が侵害されていない限り、AliceはVをBobと正しく識別した確信を一定程度得られる。その確信は次に応じる。

original_blocks.html: The availability of evidence that the transported keying material has been correctly recovered from C by Bob, e.g., through key confirmation, with Bob as the provider.

original_blocks.html: In general, Bob has no assurance that party U is Alice, since Bob has no assurance concerning the accuracy of any identifier that may be used to label party U (unless, for example, the protocol using a key-transport scheme from the KTS-OAEP family also includes additional elements that establish a trusted association between an identifier for Alice and the ciphertext, C, that she sends to Bob while acting as party U). Due to Alice’s unilateral selection of the keying material, only she can obtain assurance of its freshness. (Her level of confidence concerning its freshness is dependent upon the actual manner in which the keying material is generated by/for her.) Given that Bob simply accepts the keying material that is transported to him by Alice, he has no assurance that it is fresh. The randomized plaintext encoding used during the RSA-OAEP.ENCRYPT operation can provide assurance to Alice that the value of C will change from one KTS-OAEP transaction with Bob to the next, which may help obfuscate the occurrence of a repeated transport of the same keying material from Alice to Bob, should that ever be necessary. The KTS-OAEP-Party_V-confirmation scheme permits party V to provide evidence to party U that keying material has been correctly recovered from the ciphertext C. When the KTS-OAEP-Party_V-confirmation scheme is employed during a key-transport transaction, party V provides a key-confirmation MAC tag (MacTag ) to party U as specified in Section 9.2.4.2. This allows

original_blocks.html: The acquisition of Bob’s RSA private key by their adversary, Eve, may lead to the compromise of keying material established during past, current, and future legitimate transactions (i.e., transactions that involve honest parties and are not actively influenced by an adversary) that employ the compromised private key. For example, Eve may be able to compromise a particular KTS-OAEP transaction between Alice and Bob, as long as she also acquires the ciphertext, C, sent from Alice to Bob. In addition to compromising legitimate KTS-OAEP transactions, once Eve has learned Bob’s RSA private key, she may be able to impersonate Bob while acting as party V in future KTS-OAEP transactions (with Alice or any other party). Other schemes and applications that rely on the compromised private key may also be adversely affected. (See the discussions of other schemes in this section.) Even without knowledge of Bob’s private key, if the KTS-OAEP-Party_V-confirmation scheme is used during a particular key-transport transaction, and Eve learns the value of MacKey that Alice will send to Bob, then it may be possible for Eve to mislead Alice about Bob’s (active and successful) participation. As long as Eve also acquires the value of C intended for Bob (and any other data needed to form MacData ), it may be possible for Eve to correctly compute MacTagV V and return it to Alice as if it had come from Bob (who may not even be aware that Alice has initiated a transaction with him). Such circumstances could arise, for example, if (in violation of this Recommendation) Alice were to use the same MAC key while attempting to transport keying material to multiple parties (including both Bob and Eve).
original_blocks.html_ja: 敵対者EveがBobのRSA秘密鍵を取得すると、その侵害鍵を使う過去、現在および将来の正当なトランザクション（正直な当事者が攻撃者から能動的影響を受けずに行うトランザクション）で確立した鍵素材が侵害され得る。例えばAliceからBobに送った暗号文CもEveが入手すれば、AliceとBob間の特定のKTS-OAEPトランザクションを侵害できる場合がある。正当なKTS-OAEPトランザクションを侵害するほか、BobのRSA秘密鍵を知ったEveは、将来KTS-OAEPでVとしてBobになりすませる場合がある。他のスキームやアプリケーションも侵害された秘密鍵に依存していれば悪影響を受け得る（本節の他のスキームの説明参照）。Bobの秘密鍵を知らなくても、特定の鍵転送トランザクションでKTS-OAEP-Party_V-confirmationを用い、AliceがBobに送るMacKeyをEveが知れば、Bobが能動的かつ正常に参加したとAliceに誤信させられる場合がある。Bob宛てのC（およびMacData作成に必要な他のデータ）もEveが取得すれば、MacTag_Vを正しく計算し、Bobから来たようにAliceへ返せる場合がある（BobはAliceがトランザクションを開始したことに気付かない可能性もある）。例えば、本勧告に違反してAliceがBobとEveを含む複数相手に鍵素材を転送する際、同じMAC鍵を使った場合にこうした事態が起こり得る。

original_blocks.html: Notes: A participant in a key-establishment transaction cannot hope to distinguish between the actions of another entity and the actions of those who share knowledge of that entity’s private key-establishment key and/or any other secret data sufficient for that entity’s successful participation in a particular key-agreement transaction. In what follows, references to a “specifically identified entity” must be interpreted as an umbrella term including all those who are legitimately in possession of that entity’s private key, etc., and are trusted to act on the entity’s behalf. Any assurance obtained with respect to the actions of a specifically identified entity is conditioned upon the assumption that the identified entity’s relevant private/secret data has not been misused by a trusted party or compromised by an adversary. IKA assurance, as used in this Recommendation, does not address the potential compromise of established keying material owing to such problems as improper storage, the failure to prevent the leakage of sensitive information during computations involving the established keys, and/or inadequate methods for the timely destruction of sensitive data (including the keys themselves). These are just a few examples of misuse, mishandling, side-channel leakage, etc. that could lead to an eventual compromise. In the definition of KC assurance, this Recommendation’s requirement that it be a specifically identified entity who demonstrates the ability to use (some portion of) the established keying material is a stricter condition than is sometimes found in the literature. In this Recommendation, KC assurance presupposes IKA assurance with respect to (at least) the MAC key used in the key-confirmation computations. KC assurance can be obtained by employing a key-establishment scheme that includes key-confirmation as specified in this Recommendation. In particular, the KC provider is expected to use an RSA private key, and the KC recipient is expected to contribute random/ephemeral data that affects the values of both the MacKey and the MacData used to compute a key-confirmation MacTag.
original_blocks.html_ja: 注：鍵確立トランザクションの参加者は、他の主体と、その主体の秘密鍵確立鍵および／または当該主体の参加成功に十分な他の秘密データを共有する者の行動を区別できない。以下で「特定の識別された主体」という場合、その主体の秘密鍵などを正当に所持し、その代理として行動することを信頼された者すべてを含む包括的な用語として解釈する。本勧告で得る保証は、特定された主体の関連する秘密鍵等が信頼された者に悪用されたり攻撃者に侵害されたりしていないとの仮定に基づく。本勧告におけるIKA保証は、不適切な保存、確立済み鍵の計算中の機微情報漏えい防止の不備、機微データ（鍵自体を含む）の適時破棄方法の不備などによる確立鍵素材の侵害可能性を扱わない。これらは悪用、不適切な取扱い、サイドチャネル漏えい等を通じて最終的な侵害につながる例の一部にすぎない。KC保証の定義では、確立鍵素材の（一部を）使用できる能力を示すのが特定の識別された主体であるとの要件を置き、文献で見られる場合より厳しい条件としている。本勧告では、KC保証は鍵確認計算に用いる少なくともMAC鍵に関するIKA保証を前提とする。本勧告で規定する鍵確認を含む鍵確立スキームでKC保証を得られる。特にKC提供者はRSA秘密鍵を用い、KC受領者は鍵確認MacTag計算に用いるMacKeyとMacDataの双方の値に影響するランダム／一時データを提供することを想定する。

original_blocks.html: The following algorithm recovers the prime factors of a modulus, given the public and private exponents. The algorithm is based on Fact 1 in [Boneh 1999]. Function call: RecoverPrimeFactors(n, e, d) Input:
original_blocks.html_ja: 次のアルゴリズムは、公開指数と秘密指数から法の素因数を復元する。このアルゴリズムは[Boneh 1999]の事実1に基づく。関数呼び出し：RecoverPrimeFactors(n, e, d)。入力：

original_blocks.html: n: modulus.
original_blocks.html_ja: n：法。

original_blocks.html: e: public exponent.
original_blocks.html_ja: e：公開指数。

original_blocks.html: d: private exponent.
original_blocks.html_ja: d：秘密指数。

original_blocks.html: (p, q): prime factors of modulus.
original_blocks.html_ja: (p, q)：法の素因数。

original_blocks.html: Errors: “prime factors not found” Assumptions: The modulus n is the product of two prime factors p and q; the public and private exponents satisfy de ≡ 1 (mod λ(n)) where λ(n) = LCM(p – 1, q – 1).
original_blocks.html_ja: エラー：「素因数が見つからない」。前提条件：法nは2つの素因数pおよびqの積であり、公開指数と秘密指数はde ≡ 1 (mod λ(n))を満たす。ここでλ(n) = LCM(p − 1, q − 1)。

original_blocks.html: Let m = de – 1. If m is odd, then go to Step 4.
original_blocks.html_ja: m = de − 1とする。mが奇数ならステップ4へ進む。

original_blocks.html: Write m as m = 2tr, where r is the largest odd integer dividing m, and t ≥ 1.
original_blocks.html_ja: mをm = 2^t rと表す。ここでrはmを割り切る最大の奇数であり、t ≥ 1である。

original_blocks.html: For i = 1 to 100 do:
original_blocks.html_ja: i = 1から100まで繰り返す。

original_blocks.html: a. Generate a random integer g in the range [0, n−1]. b. Let y = gr mod n. c. If y = 1 or y = n – 1, then go to Step g. d. For j = 1 to t – 1 do:
original_blocks.html_ja: a. 範囲[0, n−1]からランダムな整数gを生成する。 b. y = g^r mod nとする。 c. y = 1またはy = n − 1ならステップgへ進む。 d. j = 1からt − 1まで繰り返す。

original_blocks.html: i. Let x = y2 mod n. ii. If x = 1, go to Step 5. iii. If x = n – 1, go to Step g. iv. Let y = x.
original_blocks.html_ja: i. x = y^2 mod nとする。 ii. x = 1ならステップ5へ進む。 iii. x = n − 1ならステップgへ進む。 iv. y = xとする。

original_blocks.html: Let p = GCD(y – 1, n) and let q = n/p.
original_blocks.html_ja: p = GCD(y − 1, n)、q = n/pとする。

original_blocks.html: Output (p, q) as the prime factors.
original_blocks.html_ja: (p, q)を素因数として出力する。

original_blocks.html: Any local copies of d, p, q , m, t, r, x, y, g and any intermediate values used during the execution of the RecoverPrimeFactors function shall be destroyed prior to or during steps 4 and 6. Note that this includes the values for p and q that are output in step 6.
original_blocks.html_ja: RecoverPrimeFactors関数の実行中に使用したd、p、q、m、t、r、x、y、gおよび中間値のローカルコピー（出力されるステップ6のpおよびqの値も含む）は、ステップ4および6の前または実行中に破棄しなければならない。

original_blocks.html: According to Fact 1 in [Boneh 1999], the probability that one of the values of y in an iteration of Step 3 reveals the factors of the modulus is at least 1/2, so on average, no more than two iterations of that step will be required. If the prime factors are not revealed after 100 iterations, then the probability is overwhelming that the modulus is not the product of two prime factors, or that the public and private exponents are not consistent with each other.
original_blocks.html_ja: [Boneh 1999]の事実1によれば、ステップ3の1回の反復において、yの値のいずれかから法の因数が得られる確率は少なくとも1/2であるため、平均して必要な反復回数は2回以下である。100回の反復後も素因数が得られない場合、法が2つの素因数の積ではないか、公開指数と秘密指数が互いに整合していない可能性が極めて高い。

original_blocks.html: The order of the recovered prime factors p and q may be the reverse of the order in which the factors were generated originally.
original_blocks.html_ja: 復元された素因数pおよびqの順序は、元の因数生成時の順序と逆になることがある。

original_blocks.html: All local copies of d, p, q, and and any other local/intermediate values used during the execution of the RecoverPrimeFactors function shall be destroyed prior to the early termination of the process due to an error, or (in the absence of errors), prior to or during the the completion of step 6.
original_blocks.html_ja: RecoverPrimeFactors関数の実行中に使用したd、p、qのすべてのローカルコピーおよびその他のローカル値／中間値は、エラーによるプロセスの早期終了前、または（エラーがない場合）ステップ6の完了前もしくは完了中に破棄しなければならない。

V Evidence that keying material has been correctly derived may be provided by using one of the three schemes from the KAS2 family that incorporates key confirmation. The KAS2-Party_V-confirmation scheme permits party V (Bob) to provide evidence of correct key derivation to party U (Alice); the KAS2-Party_U-confirmation scheme permits party U (Alice) to provide evidence of correct key derivation to party V (Bob); the KAS2-bilateral-confirmation scheme permits each party to provide evidence of correct key derivation to the other party. When the KAS2-Party_V-confirmation scheme or the KAS2-bilateral-confirmation scheme is employed during a key-agreement transaction, party V provides a key-confirmation MAC tag, MacTag , to party U as specified in Section 8.3.3.2 or Section 8.3.3.4, respectively. original_blocks.html: The acquisition of a single RSA private key by their adversary, Eve, will not (by itself) lead to the compromise of derived keying material from legitimate KAS2 transactions between Alice and Bob that employ the compromised RSA key pair. (In this context, a “legitimate transaction” is one in which Alice and Bob act honestly, and there is no active influence exerted by Eve.) However, if Eve acquires an RSA private key, she may be able to impersonate that RSA key pair’s owner while participating in KAS2 transactions. (For example, If Eve acquires Alice’s private key, she may be able to impersonate Alice – acting as party U or as party V – in KAS2 transactions with Bob or any other party). Other schemes and applications that rely on the compromised private key may also be adversely affected. (See the appropriate subsection for details.)
